answer: Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. Fingerprints are counted in nebula, as a result the distribution is public, and vine lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a signal header, so 383 keys running one model collapse to a single share. That is 7 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
